# Captured `index.ocx.sh` response bodies

Byte-exact bodies **fetched from the live production site**, not generated by
any test helper and not vendored from a golden corpus. They exist because a
wire-format drift survived for weeks with both sides' suites green: the Rust
client's tests and the `ocx-sh/index` bot's tests each pinned their own fixture,
so neither could observe that the client expected a bare `{"<ns>/<pkg>": …}` map
while the site had always served `{"format_version": …, "packages": {…}}`. A
fixture written by us can only ever confirm what we already believe. These bytes
can contradict us.

| File | Source URL | Captured | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `c-index.json` | `https://index.ocx.sh/c/index.json` | 2026-07-27 | 542 | `45a0fca769a55454eb5e20adb347a2d6770540a37b4075ebbabb81f308735690` |
| `config.json` | `https://index.ocx.sh/config.json` | 2026-07-27 | 48 | `150c9edb7627506dc8bfbb739997e362f889e0c56cc68ffc025551b4124e2a4c` |

Consumed by `tests/live_index_wire.rs`.

## Rules

- **Never hand-edit.** The point is that these are somebody else's bytes. Editing
  one to make a test pass converts it back into the kind of fixture that let the
  drift happen.
- A test here asserts only what the served shape *guarantees* — the envelope, the
  version pin, the digest-valued entries. Never the specific packages listed:
  `c/index.json` changes on every publish, and pinning its contents would make
  this a flaky test instead of a contract test.
- **Deliberately not wired to the network at test time** — same trade as
  `../index_wire/README.md`. Re-capture by hand when the served shape changes:

  ```sh
  curl -sS https://index.ocx.sh/c/index.json \
      -o crates/ocx_lib/tests/fixtures/live_index_ocx_sh/c-index.json
  curl -sS https://index.ocx.sh/config.json \
      -o crates/ocx_lib/tests/fixtures/live_index_ocx_sh/config.json
  ```

  Then update the table above and re-run `cargo test -p ocx_lib --test live_index_wire`.
